name: Naked (Uncovered) Short Call
summary: Sell a call with no underlying shares. Unlimited upside risk. Level 4 only - not permitted in this account and not offered by Alpaca at all.
max_profit: The credit received x 100, and nothing more
max_loss: UNDEFINED / UNLIMITED. Loss = (underlying at expiry - strike - credit) x 100 with no ceiling. A 100% overnight gap on a single name produces a loss many times the account equity.

greeks.gamma: negative, and it accelerates against you exactly when you are losing

when_to_use: Never in this account. Documented for completeness and so the system can classify and refuse it. Institutionally it is only run with continuous delta hedging and hard risk limits.
entry_rules: BLOCKED: requires Level 4. This account is Level 3 (Alpaca PAPER, ~$50k equity), and Alpaca does not offer Level 4 to retail traders - its approval tiers run 1 through 3 only. Any such order will be rejected by the broker
The automation must refuse to construct this order rather than relying on broker rejection, so that rejected-order noise never masks a real problem
Any short call that exists with zero covering shares and no long call at a higher strike is naked by definition and must be flattened immediately
management_rules: Reference discipline if it were ever permitted: close at 50% of credit, hard stop at 2x credit, mandatory close if delta exceeds 0.30, never hold through earnings
exit_rules: Any detected uncovered short call is bought to close at market immediately, regardless of time of day or P&L
No never-assign timer applies, because the position must not exist for longer than it takes to flatten it
assignment_risk: EXTREME and unbounded. Early assignment creates a short stock position of unlimited risk, subject to buy-in, borrow fees and dividend liability, in an account not approved for it.
buying_power: Level 4 naked call margin: the greater of (20% of underlying value - OTM amount + premium) or (10% of underlying value + premium). Unavailable here.
common_mistakes: Assuming a far-OTM short call is safe. Single-name gap risk is the entire reason this approval level exists.
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
